- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to match true decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–3% downward bias for 5–7 days if price is above 10-day moving average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–4% in the first 10 days; apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 5 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.67 → -0.67), model often misjudges direction; add a 1–3% downward adjustment for next 3–5 days.
